d: Opt in to platform-integrated TextChatService so Roblox delivers and renders chat messages with TextChannelWindow.
h:
Starting in May 2027, platform-integrated chat will be required for all games. The unsupported APIs will be deprecated, and custom chat will have to use the new TextChatService features.

When you enable platform-integrated chat, custom chat features must move to Roblox's native systems (TextChatCommands, TextChannelWindow, Quick Words). Message content is also no longer accessible in code.

Platform-integrated chat gives every player consistent access to safety tools such as reporting and muting, and lets chat features like Quick Words roll out reliably across all games. It also replaces the current prefix system, so roles associated with users render consistently and are safe for all ages.

Nothing in your game changes until you enable platform-integrated chat in Studio. After you enable it:

  • Roblox delivers and renders chat in the default window or a TextChannelWindow you place in your UI. Custom chat UIs can no longer render messages themselves.
  • Player message text isn't accessible to your code. You can't read, log, or export it. APIs that previously returned message text now return an empty string ("") instead of nil, so your scripts keep running but receive no content.

Commands triggered from chat must use TextChatCommand.

Unsupported APIs

When platform-integrated chat is enabled, the following APIs return "" (empty string, not nil) and log a warning:

Feature Unsupported APIs What to use instead
Chat messages and display TextChatMessage.Text, TextChatMessage.Translation Migrate your custom chat GUI to TextChannelWindow. Set Target to a TextChannel. Users can send and receive messages automatically.
Chat prefixes TextChatMessage.PrefixText Not supported. If your game requires prefixes, don't enable platform-integrated chat yet.
Presets / chat wheels TextChannel:SendAsync() Use [Quick Words](#/docs/chat/quick-words) creator customization to add relevant phrases to chat.
Moderation / admin commands OnIncomingMessage, Player.Chatted Use TextChatCommand for chat-triggered commands. Use read-only chat to view all chats for moderation during live events.

Enable platform-integrated chat

To enable platform-integrated chat in Studio:

  1. Open the Explorer window.
  2. Select TextChatService.
  3. In the Properties panel, find PlatformIntegratedChat.
  4. Set it to Enabled.

With the update enabled, the unsupported APIs listed earlier return empty strings and log warnings. You can set the property back to Disabled at any time to revert.

You can only change this property in Studio, not from a script.

Create a TextChannelWindow

To create a TextChannelWindow:

  1. Create a ScreenGui in StarterGui.
  2. Add a TextChannelWindow instance as a child of the ScreenGui.
  3. Set the Size and Position properties to place the window where you want it.
  4. Set the Target property to the TextChannel you want the window to display.

Each TextChannelWindow binds to a single TextChannel. To show multiple channels together, create a TextChannelWindow for each channel and apply your own show/hide logic. The Global channel isn't available as a target for a custom window.

The following code sample creates a custom chat window that displays the RBXGeneral channel:

LocalScript in StarterGui

local TextChatService = game:GetService("TextChatService")

local screenGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screenGui.Name = "TextChannelWindowDemo"
screenGui.Parent = script.Parent

local myTextChannelWindow = Instance.new("TextChannelWindow")
myTextChannelWindow.Size = UDim2.new(0, 400, 0, 300)
myTextChannelWindow.Position = UDim2.new(0, 10, 0, 10)
myTextChannelWindow.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(20, 20, 20)
myTextChannelWindow.BackgroundTransparency = 0.5

local targetChannelName = "RBXGeneral"
local targetChannel = TextChatService:WaitForChild("TextChannels"):WaitForChild(targetChannelName)

if targetChannel and targetChannel:IsA("TextChannel") then
    myTextChannelWindow.Target = targetChannel
end

myTextChannelWindow.Parent = screenGui

Show a custom channel only in its own window

By default, the default chat window renders messages from every TextChannel, so a channel you show in a custom TextChannelWindow also appears in the default window.

To show a custom channel only in its own window:

  1. In the Explorer, select ChatWindowConfiguration under TextChatService.
  2. In the Properties panel, set TextChannelDisplayMode to DefaultTextChannels.
  3. For each custom channel, create a TextChannelWindow and set its Target to that channel.

The following example shows a custom Guild channel that appears only in its own window:

LocalScript in StarterPlayerScripts

-- Prerequisite: TextChannelDisplayMode is set to DefaultTextChannels in Studio.
local TextChatService = game:GetService("TextChatService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local playerGui = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

-- Scripts can read the property at runtime, but can't change it.
local config = TextChatService.ChatWindowConfiguration
if config.TextChannelDisplayMode ~= Enum.TextChannelDisplayMode.DefaultTextChannels then
    warn("Guild messages will also appear in the default chat window.")
end

local guildChannel = TextChatService:WaitForChild("TextChannels"):WaitForChild("Guild")

local screenGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screenGui.Name = "GuildChat"
screenGui.Parent = playerGui

local guildWindow = Instance.new("TextChannelWindow")
guildWindow.Size = UDim2.new(0, 400, 0, 300)
guildWindow.Target = guildChannel
guildWindow.Parent = screenGui

Keep these behaviors in mind:

  • You can set TextChannelDisplayMode only in Studio or from a plugin. Scripts can read it at runtime but can't change it.
  • The property exists only on ChatWindowConfiguration. TextChannelWindow doesn't need it because it already shows a single channel through Target.
  • Channels created at runtime follow the current mode when they appear. Default channels created at runtime, such as Team and Whisper, still appear in the default window.

Migrate chat-triggered admin commands

Whether you need to update your admin commands depends on how they are triggered:

  • Commands triggered from chat must use TextChatCommand.
  • Command handling that reads raw chat text no longer works. This includes MessageReceived, Chatted, or anything else that inspects TextChatMessage content.

To migrate:

  1. Identify admin commands in your game that currently parse raw chat messages.
  2. Create a TextChatCommand for each command.
  3. Define the command's trigger keyword and callback logic.
  4. Remove any code that reads Text or listens to Chatted for command handling.

For an example, see Custom text chat commands.

FAQ

Will anything change if I do nothing?

Nothing changes in your game unless you set PlatformIntegratedChat to Enabled.

Does this affect signs, boards, notes, or other in-world text players can write?

No. Policy for those surfaces is unchanged: they can't be used for two-way communication between players, they need rate limiting of at least 1 minute, and they are subject to moderation.

Does this affect comment systems, message boards, or mail in my game?

No. This update covers TextChatService only.

Can I still record and pull chat logs as a game admin?

No. When PlatformIntegratedChat is Enabled, no API returns player message content on the client or server. Moderators in your game can still use read-only chat permissions to view chat. Players can also rely on Roblox's abuse reporting and on safety tools such as muting and blocking.

Do I need to change anything if I use the default Roblox chat?

No. If your game uses the default Roblox chat with no customizations, you don't need to take action and shouldn't see a change.

kid.simple: Platform-integrated chat is a new mode where Roblox itself shows and delivers all chat messages. When you turn it on, your scripts can no longer read what players type. That keeps everyone safer and makes safety tools work the same in every game. Starting in May 2027 every game will need it, so it is smart to learn it now.
kid.analogy: It is like a mail carrier who delivers sealed letters. You can choose where the mailbox goes and what it looks like, but you are not allowed to open the letters.
keyPoints: Nothing changes until you set `TextChatService.PlatformIntegratedChat` to Enabled in Studio. You can set it back to Disabled any time.
You can only change this setting in Studio, not from a script.
Once enabled, message text APIs like `TextChatMessage.Text` return an empty string `""` instead of the message, and log a warning.
To show chat in your own UI, use a `TextChannelWindow` and set its `Target` to a `TextChannel`. Each window shows one channel.
Chat prefixes (`PrefixText`) are not supported. If your game needs them, do not enable this yet.
Chat commands must use `TextChatCommand`. Code that reads `Player.Chatted` or message text to find commands stops working.
To keep a custom channel out of the default window, set `ChatWindowConfiguration.TextChannelDisplayMode` to DefaultTextChannels in Studio.
If you just use the default Roblox chat with no changes, you do not need to do anything.

terms.platform-integrated: Built into Roblox itself. Roblox, not your game, handles showing and sending the messages.
terms.TextChannelWindow: A UI object that shows the messages of one chat channel. You choose its size and position, Roblox fills in the messages.
terms.TextChannel: One chat room, like `RBXGeneral` (everyone) or a custom one like `Guild`.
terms.Target: The property on a `TextChannelWindow` that says which `TextChannel` it shows.
terms.empty string: Text with nothing in it, written `""`. It is different from `nil`, so your scripts keep running but just get no words.
terms.deprecated: Old and on its way out. It may still work for now, but you should stop using it.
terms.prefix: A tag shown before a player's name in chat, like `[VIP]`. Not supported with platform-integrated chat.
terms.TextChatCommand: An object that makes a slash command like `/kick` run your code, without your code needing to read the message text.
terms.read-only chat: A permission that lets moderators view chat during live events without any API giving the text to scripts.

example.title: Show the main chat in your own window
example.code:
local TextChatService = game:GetService("TextChatService")

-- Make a ScreenGui to hold the window
local screenGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screenGui.Name = "MyChatGui"
screenGui.Parent = script.Parent

-- Make the chat window: 400 pixels wide, 300 tall, 10 pixels from the top-left corner
local chatWindow = Instance.new("TextChannelWindow")
chatWindow.Size = UDim2.new(0, 400, 0, 300)
chatWindow.Position = UDim2.new(0, 10, 0, 10)
chatWindow.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(20, 20, 20)
chatWindow.BackgroundTransparency = 0.5

-- Find the general channel and show it in the window
local channels = TextChatService:WaitForChild("TextChannels")
local general = channels:WaitForChild("RBXGeneral")
chatWindow.Target = general

chatWindow.Parent = screenGui
explain: We get `TextChatService`, which runs the chat.
We create a `ScreenGui` so the window can appear on the player's screen.
We create a `TextChannelWindow` and give it a size and a spot on the screen.
We wait for the `RBXGeneral` channel, which is the normal everyone-can-see chat.
Setting `Target` tells the window which channel to show. Roblox then fills in and sends messages for us.
Last, we parent the window to the `ScreenGui` so it shows up.

watchOut: Trying to log or save chat messages after enabling it. No API gives you the message text anymore, on the client or the server.
Building admin commands by reading `Player.Chatted`. Use `TextChatCommand` instead, or the commands will stop working.
Trying to show the Global channel in a custom `TextChannelWindow`. That is not allowed.
Trying to change `TextChannelDisplayMode` from a script. Scripts can only read it. Set it in Studio.
Forgetting that your custom channel also shows in the default window unless you change `TextChannelDisplayMode`.
